findings.says: `CurrencyCode` includes perfectly into 2 different keys — which is THE reference?
evidence: measured on 4 reference(s) across 2 relation(s) (orders, sales): inclusion is 1.0 into every one of currencyexchange.FromCurrency, currencyexchange.ToCurrency, at the same key role and over the same rows. Value inclusion CANNOT separate them, so neither was drawn as the sole reference.
findings.needs: Which of currencyexchange.FromCurrency, currencyexchange.ToCurrency is THE reference for CurrencyCode?  ANSWER ONE OF: currencyexchange.FromCurrency | currencyexchange.ToCurrency | both_are_real | neither.  No recommendation is offered from the data because the data cannot carry one.
remedies: currencyexchange.FromCurrency: CurrencyCode references currencyexchange.FromCurrency, the reference to currencyexchange.ToCurrency is recorded as rejected-by-ruling, and questions convert FROM the order's currency. IF THE CHOICE IS WRONG THE NUMBERS DO NOT ERROR — they come back transformed the wrong way and still look plausible, which is the hardest defect to find later.

currencyexchange.ToCurrency: CurrencyCode references currencyexchange.ToCurrency, the reference to currencyexchange.FromCurrency is recorded as rejected-by-ruling, and questions convert INTO the order's currency. IF THE CHOICE IS WRONG THE NUMBERS DO NOT ERROR — they come back transformed the wrong way and still look plausible, which is the hardest defect to find later.
both_are_real: two references are drawn and every traversal must say which it used; a question that does not name a direction becomes ambiguous rather than wrong.
neither: CurrencyCode stays an attribute, no line is drawn, and no question can traverse from it — the join must be written by hand each time, where it is visible.
findings.recommended: the endpoint the child is DENOMINATED IN — for an amount and an FX rate table, the child column is the `from` side

findings.says: `CategoryKey` is key-shaped and no relation in scope carries it as a key
evidence: reported on 1 plane-relation(s) (product 8 distinct); 8 distinct value(s) on product. It follows this bundle's own key-naming convention and points at nothing.
findings.needs: Is the parent MISSING from the extract, already INLINE on the row, or is CategoryKey just an attribute?  ANSWER ONE OF: inline_dimension | attribute_only | missing_extract.  RECOMMENDED: inline_dimension — product.CategoryName carries the SAME 8 distinct value(s) as CategoryKey, dense over 1..8 — the label already travels with the key, so a concept grounds on product and no parent relation is needed at all
remedies: inline_dimension: a concept is grounded on the carrying relation, using the key for identity and its twin for the label; no parent relation is ever needed and no line is drawn
attribute_only: CategoryKey is an opaque identifier and nothing groups by it — questions use the denormalised attributes beside it instead
missing_extract: the extract is incomplete and it is recorded as such; until the dimension arrives, anything grouped by this key can report only opaque values, and every answer over it must say so

findings.says: `sales` re-delivers every line of `orderrows` — one fact, twice
evidence: 223,974 rows each. `sales` carries all but 1 column of `orderrows` (RowNumber is spelled differently there), plus 7: CurrencyCode, CustomerKey, DeliveryDate, ExchangeRate, LineNumber, OrderDate, StoreKey. So `sales` answers at this grain with NO join, and `orderrows` cannot answer at all without a header relation. Only one is served, so the ambiguity is latent rather than live.
findings.needs: Which is the FACT OF RECORD?  ANSWER ONE OF: orderrows | sales | both_are_distinct_facts | neither_serve_a_transform.  RECOMMENDED: serve exactly ONE — see the ruling.
remedies: orderrows: the normalised detail is the record, and every question at this grain must JOIN a header relation to reach the attributes `sales` already carries. `sales` must STOP being served, or the ambiguity remains whatever is declared.
sales: the pre-joined relation is the record and answers with no join, including the 7 attributes the normalised route reaches only through a header. `orderrows` must stop being served.

both_are_distinct_facts: each is declared a fact in its own right, which requires a reason the measurement contradicts — they agree row for row — and every total over them becomes a sum a reader must know not to take twice.

neither_serve_a_transform: a curated relation is authored over one of them and BOTH landings stop being served — the route a curated bundle took, which is available here and is what the passthrough cannot do for you.

findings.says: served relation `contoso5_brand` is claimed by no concept
evidence: 22 relation(s) are served and 8 are claimed by at least one of 11 concept(s); `contoso5_brand` is claimed by none. A served relation is one a question can read, so an unclaimed one is either a notion nobody modelled or a relation that should not be served — and the delivered artifacts do not say which.
findings.needs: Which is it?  ANSWER ONE OF: model_a_concept | stop_serving_it | backs_no_notion.  A decline is a legitimate answer and the reason is the deliverable — `backs_no_notion` with no reason leaves the next reader exactly where this finding found them.
remedies: model_a_concept: a concept grounds on it and the relation becomes answerable
stop_serving_it: it leaves the served plane — which on a 1:1 passthrough means authoring a transform, because a passthrough serves everything by construction
backs_no_notion: it stays served and is recorded as deliberately unmodelled, so the next reader finds the decision instead of the gap

said.words: RULED BY ROLE ontology-developer UNDER EXPLICIT TASK DIRECTION (2026-10-16 register->relation fold completion), NOT A STANDING OPERATOR SIGN-OFF ON THIS BUNDLE'S MODEL — flagged here for operator review/override. MEASURED, not the three stock answers: `Brand` already serves this exact value (`dim_product.brand`, in `Brand`'s own grounding), so this is neither an unmodelled notion (`model_a_concept`) nor a notion with none (`backs_no_notion`) — it is ALREADY modelled, one relation over. The register is the FK domain `dim_product.brand` draws from (and, where shared, what other relations' own `brand`-shaped columns draw from too), not a second ground for `Brand`. Declining to bind it as a second `grounding.bindings[]` entry: `check_delivery_consistency._effective_source` reads only a concept's FIRST binding, so a second entry would not even register as 'claimed' by this gate, and restructuring `Brand`'s primary binding onto this narrower, differently-named register would drop columns and rules bound to the richer relation's own column names for no gain. `Brand` also carries `counts: brand` — 11 distinct values over 2517 product rows, exactly this register's 11 rows.

said.words: RULED BY ROLE ontology-developer UNDER EXPLICIT TASK DIRECTION (2026-10-23, the operator's ruling that the KPI channel split belongs in the transformation layer), NOT A STANDING OPERATOR SIGN-OFF ON THIS BUNDLE'S MODEL — flagged here for operator review/override. MEASURED, and the answer is `backs_no_notion` rather than `model_a_concept`: THE CHANNEL IS ALREADY MODELLED, AS A READING AND NOT AS AN ENTITY. `Store.channel` declares it as a POPULATION AXIS on Store with two named populations (`physical`, `online`), and `v_contoso5_sales_line.channel` now carries the same split as a column on the FACT so that no question has to reach the store dimension to learn it. A `Channel` CONCEPT existed and was DELIBERATELY DELETED — acceptance/prompts/*.txt still carry it as history — because a channel is not a thing you can count, it is which rows a question is about. This relation is the closed DOMAIN that column draws from (`references: contoso5_channel.code`), never a second ground: binding a concept to it would make a THIRD home for one fact, beside the population rule and the fact column, which is the defect the 2026-10-15 register fold exists to prevent. AND IT IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, unlike its twelve siblings: the values come from a CASE expression with exactly two branches, so no delivery can add a third without editing the transform — the others are cut from a stored column and are closed only as far as today's rows go.

findings.says: served relation `contoso5_color` is claimed by no concept
evidence: 22 relation(s) are served and 8 are claimed by at least one of 11 concept(s); `contoso5_color` is claimed by none. A served relation is one a question can read, so an unclaimed one is either a notion nobody modelled or a relation that should not be served — and the delivered artifacts do not say which.
findings.needs: Which is it?  ANSWER ONE OF: model_a_concept | stop_serving_it | backs_no_notion.  A decline is a legitimate answer and the reason is the deliverable — `backs_no_notion` with no reason leaves the next reader exactly where this finding found them.
remedies: model_a_concept: a concept grounds on it and the relation becomes answerable
stop_serving_it: it leaves the served plane — which on a 1:1 passthrough means authoring a transform, because a passthrough serves everything by construction
backs_no_notion: it stays served and is recorded as deliberately unmodelled, so the next reader finds the decision instead of the gap

said.words: RULED BY ROLE ontology-developer UNDER EXPLICIT TASK DIRECTION (2026-10-16 register->relation fold completion), NOT A STANDING OPERATOR SIGN-OFF ON THIS BUNDLE'S MODEL — flagged here for operator review/override.
